subject: Anthropology
title: Dendrochronology
description: A quick, practical guide to Dendrochronology.

hook.text: A tree adds one ring per year. Count the rings and you know its age. Match patterns and you can date buildings.

buildup.text: Dendrochronology dates wood by matching its ring patterns to a master sequence built from overlapping tree samples.

discovery.text: It can date wooden beams, ship timbers, and charcoal to the exact year — far more precise than radiocarbon.

twist.text: Ring width also records climate. Narrow rings mean drought. Dendrochronology is both a clock and a weather diary.

climax.text: Tree rings connect archaeology to climate history, showing how droughts and cold spells shaped human civilizations.

punchline.text: Trees recorded history before humans could write.

quiz.question: What makes dendrochronology precise?
options: It uses chemical analysis of soil
It matches tree ring patterns to date wood to exact years

details.summary: Dendrochronology uses tree-ring patterns to date wood to the exact calendar year. Since trees produce rings of varying width depending on growing conditions, matching ring patterns creates continuous chronologies extending thousands of years into the past.
details.whyItMatters: Dendrochronology is the most precise archaeological dating method available, accurate to a single year. It also calibrates radiocarbon dates and reconstructs past climate, making it indispensable for archaeology and environmental history.
takeaways: Tree rings can date wood to the exact calendar year
Ring patterns are matched to create multi-thousand-year chronologies
Dendrochronology calibrates radiocarbon dates and reconstructs climate

faq.question: How far back does dendrochronology extend?
faq.answer: Continuous tree-ring chronologies extend over 12,000 years in some regions by overlapping patterns from living trees, historical timbers, and subfossil wood. This provides an independent check on radiocarbon dating and reconstructs annual climate variations.

faq.question: What are the limitations of dendrochronology?
faq.answer: It requires preserved wood with intact rings, works only in regions with seasonal climate variation, and needs existing reference chronologies. Tropical trees without distinct annual rings cannot be dated this way. Available reference chronologies vary by region.
